rows.evidence: Q1: Methods and Results, Table 1 <U+2014> the authors train AlexNet and GoogLeNet on 54,306 PlantVillage leaf images across 60 experimental configurations and report their own held-out test accuracies (up to 99.35%) and accuracies on two small external image sets (~31%).
rows.notes: The study classifies single, upward-facing leaf images taken under controlled conditions (and some web-sourced leaf photos) into crop-disease classes; it is not remote sensing or UAV imagery, and it only classifies the presence/identity of disease on an already symptomatic leaf. It does not grade severity, does not test detection before canopy-wide symptoms, and reports nothing on targeted responses or pest control. The authors themselves state the approach is limited to single leaves on homogeneous backgrounds and that early-stage visual diagnosis is challenging. Detection is at most a precondition of the claimed control effect, and the imaging technology differs from the one in the passage.

notes: Full text appears complete. Study is a deep-learning image classification benchmark on leaf photographs (PlantVillage), with no field, canopy-scale, UAV or disease-management component.
